title: semantic-ownership-ambiguous-at-composition-seam

proposition.statement: A relying system must not resolve a material semantic fact across a composition seam when the competent owner of that fact, or an explicit reconciliation rule between participating specifications, cannot be established.

preconditions: Two or more specifications or components contribute to a composed decision.
A material fact such as authority, completion, status, acceptance, or policy applicability affects the relying proposition.
Ownership of that fact is ambiguous, overlapping, or unstated and no explicit reconciliation rule establishes which source governs.

trigger.statement: The composed system selects, synthesizes, or infers a value for the material fact and returns a relying result as though semantic ownership were established.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence identifying the competent authority, if authority determines ownership of the material fact.
Evidence identifying the applicable rule for semantic ownership or reconciliation across the seam.
Evidence describing the participating components and the semantic contract at their boundary.
Evidence showing which component or authority produced the material fact relied upon.

falsification.condition: The system returns PASS after choosing between overlapping semantic claims without an explicit competent owner or reconciliation rule.
A component is treated as owner of a material fact solely because it produced the most convenient or most recent value.

references.note: Repository judgment record for this failure proposition.
